chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Bands on the furniture wagons: Kelly, Morgan, Collins, Rena
summary: On Sundays bands rode rented dray wagons, and Danny lists the bands he saw as a boy of 10 to 12.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Then you heard of Sundays. Sunday you would see them great bands on the wagons, on the tailgate the trombone and that bass would sit there, and you would look to see who that was. And about midway(?) the wagon... They used furniture wagons, which was a long wagon. You've seen them. They're trucks, but they're laid on the... All that comes in a big van. But the little one... The furniture stores used to have a long wagon, maybe about 15 feet long, that they'd put mattresses on, the mattress and the bed. You don't see those wagons. But they used to use them and rent them from the furniture store. They had some guys who was draymen who rented wagons... It was a big business, what do you say, a drayman, because you could go in and rent different kinds of
carts if you wanted to haul something. Like a U-Haul today. You'd go in and hire a horse-and-wagon from Mister So-and-So. He's got the drayman's yard.

So they'd rent them wagons, then you'd see on the front... You'd see Chris Kelly's band, you'd see Sam Morgan's band, you'd see Lee Collins' band, Kid Rena's band. At that time, when I was coming up, when I was kid around 10 and 11 and 12, you'd see the Chameleon Band and you'd see the Olympia Band. And sometimes I'd see a band that I'd never see no more. There would be some band come out of a little country town, and it would be Slidedale(?) or one of them little country towns -- and all of them had bands. And all of them played the tradition without a piano. That way you could sing, because the piano would be out of tune, and you don't want to fool around with a piano that's out of tune, and it hasn't been used when it's been there, and the keys is out...
